newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER-SHERINGHAM DOUBLE GIVES ENGLAND VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER-SHERINGHAM DOUBLE GIVES ENGLAND VICTORY.

text.p: Teddy Sheringham and Alan Shearer rekindled memories of Euro 96 when they scored a goal each to give England a hard-earned 2-0 victory over Georgia in a World Cup qualifier at Wembley on Wednesday.
The two forwards had not played together since the June championship when they hit seven goals between them to become the tournament's most potent striking force.
But their mutual understanding was evident on Wednesday as each one set up a goal for the other.
Sheringham, who scored against Georgia in Tbilisi last November before missing England's 1-0 home defeat by Italy in February through injury, put England ahead three minutes before halftime.
Shearer played the role of provider, picking the ball up on the left flank and crossing for Sheringham to thump home a header from close range.
The score remained at 1-0 until second half injury-time when the two men swapped roles.
Sheringham, so often the provider for his team mates both at Spurs and England, back-heeled a close-range indirect free-kick to Shearer who blasted the ball high into the roof of the Georgia net.
Seconds later the whistle went, giving England a result which keeps them in sight of group two leaders Italy, who beat Poland 3-0 in Naples.

"I don't think we deserved to win 2-0 but we got our noses in front and managed to stay there," said Sheringham, who praised a spirited an inventive Georgia side who always looked capable of pulling themselves back into the match.
England coach Glenn Hoddle was more upbeat about his side's performance.

"I was very pleased with the first half. We had good movement and good chances and the goal was magnificent. My disappointment was in the 20 minutes after that. We should have got the second earlier and then we could have punished them."

Georgia created the first chance of the evening when the impressive Temur Ketsbaia, who recently signed up to join English side Newcastle next season, put Shota Arveladze in on goal only for Spurs defender Sol Campbell to make a crucial tackle.

Hoddle's side took control, using the width of the Wembley pitch to full advantage and relying heavily on wing-back Graeme Le Saux on the left and the young Manchester United pairing of David Beckham and Gary Neville on the right.
Sheringham headed an early chance just wide of Irakil Zoidze's left-hand post and Robert Lee blasted a shot inches over the upright mid-way through the half.
Minutes later a Lee cross from the left grazed the Georgia crossbar and Beckham's follow-up shot was blocked in the six- yard box.
For all England's good work on the wings though, the heart of Georgia's disciplined defence held firm until Sheringham finally broke the deadlock.
To their credit, Georgia took the initiative straight after the restart and, with Manchester City's Giorgi Kinkladze working his magic in midfield, they could easily have found an equaliser.
England keeper David Seaman was forced to make a fine save with his legs after a poor back pass from Le Saux had gifted the ball to Georgia's first half substitute Gocha Gogrichiani.

And Georgia captain Kakhi Tskhadadze, who was outstanding at the heart of his defence, skimmed a shot off the top of Seaman's crossbar as the visitors strived to find thier first goal -- and point -- of the current World Cup campaign.
England held on though and Shearer's late strike -- following an ill-advised back-pass -- sealed a result which keeps England on course for at least second place in their qualifying group.
